claims.statement: The production stack is one compose network of 18 services: eight built images, eight per-service Redis instances, postgres-feedback and rabbitmq-feedback, with data in bind-mounted apps/*/data directories and named volumes for infra.

A fresh checkout has no apps/*/data directories (gitignored); they must exist and be owned by 1000:1000 before `up`, or Docker creates them root-owned and the uid-1000 images cannot open their SQLite files.

Required env vars have no code fallback by design (a guessed port half-succeeds a write), so arch-check RULE 6 enforces that every variable a service reads is forwarded in its own compose environment block.

Backup/restore CLIs live in @life/db: db:backup/db:restore cover the six SQLite stores (with --pin producing backup/<utc-stamp>-pinned/ snapshots) and db:backup:pg/db:restore:pg cover the feedback Postgres database.
The deploy ordering rule is absolute: back up → migrate → boot, never migrate after boot, and never `docker compose down -v` during a backup window because -v removes redis-app-data (sessions).
Production deploys, data migrations, data directories, secrets and ports are human hard lines: run with the runbook's checklist, never automated.
